m0027:
■ Publication Scope
Data is saved immediately only if the server has the same address and certificate fingerprint as the common lookup server used by this app, and if that server has directly authorized the publication. In all other cases, an approval code from the common server ID lookup service administrator is required, and automatic approval is not granted. Use the [Advanced] Connection Name/Publish tab.
m0028:
■ How to obtain the server admin key
1) If you only want to join a server, you do not need its admin key. Enter the server ID and server password provided by its owner in [Join server].
m0029:
■ Existing IDs
You can continue to use your existing IDs, and you can keep up to 8 of them. We do not support deleting IDs or transferring them to other servers.
m0030:
■ Distinguishing It from Other Values
- This is not your AWS account password or SSH password.
- It is also different from the participation password entered by participants.
m0031:
■ Distinguishing Between Different Names
- Display Name: A name stored on the server by the server owner for display purposes
- Server Name (Connection Settings): A local profile name unique to this PC
- Access Name (Alias): A directory alias that participants enter when joining
These three values are distinct from one another, and changing one does not affect the others. The display name is not the same as the account ID.
m0032:
■ Change Procedure
1) Enter the server management key and click [Authenticate / View Current Settings].
2) Enter a new display name.
3) If it is the same server, the management key will remain hidden in this window (if it is blank, re-enter it), so click [Save Settings].
m0033:
■ Storage Method (Input Memory)
[Input Memory] is enabled by default. When enabled, the management key, server ID, server password, and server ID for participation (ID/PW) are encrypted and stored so that they can only be decrypted by the current Windows user account on this PC. Saved values are only re-entered for exactly the same connection settings (address, full fingerprint, and the same server ID for participation) and are always unverified drafts. Saved entries do not constitute authentication or proof of ownership, and do not trigger automatic participation, automatic queries, or automatic server calls. The restored server password will not be transmitted again unless you manually edit it.
Selecting [Delete Saved Input] or turning off [Remember Input] clears only the current connection settings for the current role (device registration, connection history, and other roles are retained). There is no export function, and data cannot be transferred to external documents or other PCs. If the server ID you previously joined points to a different server, the password will not be sent; if it is the correct new server, please delete the saved input and re-enter the password.
The management key displayed on the screen is used only for the connection settings at the time of entry and will be cleared from the screen if the connection settings change.
m0034:
■ How to Use
Click [Copy Access Name] to copy the access name, then provide it along with the participation password to the participants separately so they can [Join].
m0035:
■ Server Password
This is the password used to log in to the server (8–128 characters; include leading and trailing spaces as is). If left blank, the existing password will be retained. Passwords stored on the server cannot be retrieved.
If [Remember Input] is enabled, a draft of the server ID and password is stored in encrypted form on this Windows user account (unverified draft; not a credential). The restored password will not be transmitted until you edit it yourself, and the ability to copy it will not be restored. To delete, select [Delete Saved Input] (current role only).
m0036:
■ Setup Procedure
1) Enter a new participant password consisting of 8 to 128 characters.
2) If the server management key field at the top is blank, enter a value (on the same server, this field remains hidden behind this window).
3) Click [Save Settings] and verify the success message at the bottom.
After submitting to the server, the input fields will be cleared for security reasons; they may also be cleared if the submission fails. Do not assume the operation was successful simply because the values have disappeared. If the submission is blocked before submission due to a missing management key or a format error, the new participation password will be retained.
m0037:
■ Servers with the "Owner" feature enabled
There is no additional password. Simply enter the server password (participation password) specified in [Server ID / PW] as is.
m0038:
■ What is not an authorization code
It is not a random string, a server management key, a participant password, or an administrator key.
m0039:
■ Where to obtain it
- For your own server: run the command below on that server using its public certificate.
- For someone else's server: obtain the fingerprint directly from its owner by phone or in person.
Command for the server owner:
openssl x509 -in /etc/peerdesk/server.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
Remove the colons from the output and use the resulting 64-character value.
m0040:
■ Where to obtain the address
For a server you installed, use the server computer’s public IP address or domain and its configured port (for example, 8443). For someone else’s server, ask its owner for the address. Only the server owner enters the address; participants do not. Creating an AWS instance alone is not enough: the RemoteBridge server must be running on that instance, with the required port accessible.

■ Note
- Changing the participation password does not automatically unregister the device.
- The new server version stores device registrations in a file. Even if you restart the server or the app, the same PC ID is retained; only a new temporary password is issued.
- When upgrading from an older server for the first time, you must rejoin once. If you delete or reset the server’s registration file or this PC’s registration information, or if you change your Windows account, the same ID is not guaranteed. The ID is not calculated based on the MAC address.
m0062:
■ Initial Posting Procedure
1) Choose the access name and connection settings (address, full fingerprint) you want to use.
2) Request approval for the new access name from the Common Name Lookup Service administrator. This version does not include a screen for automatically issuing approval codes.
3) Enter the approval code received by the server owner, enter the server management key, and then click [Publish Server Name].
4) Check the publication results via [Verify Access Name].
5) Separately provide the verified access name and participation password to participants.

■ Deactivate
Select a device from the list, ensure the server management key is entered (re-enter it if it is blank), and then click [Unregister Selected Device]. This will invalidate the device’s authentication token and disconnect any active connections. To use the device again, you must re-register it. If you unregister your own PC, you will need to rejoin the session.

This screen is for the server owner (the person who set up the server). Users who are simply joining the server do not need this screen; they just need to enter the server ID and server password provided by the server owner in the [Join Server] field.

1) Enter the HTTPS address and the full certificate fingerprint (64 characters) of the RemoteBridge server that is already running. If you installed the server yourself, enter your own server’s values; if it is someone else’s server, enter the values provided by that server owner. Simply creating an AWS instance does not install the server.

2) After clicking [Verify Server Connection], authenticate using the management key you set during server installation (or the key provided by the server owner if it’s someone else’s server). Server management is possible without registering a PC.

3) In the [Server ID / Password] section, set and save the server ID and password you wish to share. The server name lookup feature will save the information immediately only if the server owner has explicitly allowed direct publishing. Otherwise, an approval code from the administrator of the shared server ID lookup service is required. Approval is not granted simply because you are an app distributor or server owner, and it is not automatically approved.

4) Provide the saved server ID and server password to the other party. If you also wish to use remote connections, register your PC under [Join Server].

The address is the public IP or domain of the computer where the server is installed (e.g., Lightsail instance details), along with the installation port (e.g., 8443). Verify the fingerprint directly on your own server using the OpenSSL command described in the [Certificate Fingerprint] help section, or if it’s another server, obtain it from the server owner via a separate method, such as by phone or in person. The public profile file itself is not proof of trust.

The local profile name, JSON source, and previous server invitation code are advanced settings. New servers use the server password without requiring an additional invitation code. New-version servers store PC registration information in a file, so they retain the same ID even after restarting the server or app. You may need to rejoin once after initially switching to the new version. Any active remote connections will be terminated when the server restarts, and a new temporary password will be issued.
